headline: Samsunspor chase an unwanted record as Amed visit
summary: Samsunspor have lost six Süper Lig games in a row, and Turkish media report that a seventh on Saturday would be a club record. New coach Nenad Bjelica lost his first match in charge 4-1 at Kasımpaşa, and the side are 17th with four points. Amed are second and unbeaten in five, though both away games in that run finished 2-2. Amed are narrow favourites at 40.7% to Samsunspor's 32.2%, with a handicap of only a quarter of a goal.
read: Samsunspor are second from bottom on six straight league defeats, with a new coach still waiting for his first point and a club-record seventh loss in sight. Amed arrive second and unbeaten in five, and the market makes them favourites — though only about a quarter of a goal better, with the 2.5-goal line split down the middle.

sources.fact: Samsunspor have lost six Süper Lig matches in a row and sit 17th with 4 points from 8 games, per Turkish media.
Turkish media report that a defeat to Amed would give Samsunspor a seventh straight loss, a new club record for their longest losing run.
Nenad Bjelica took over as Samsunspor coach after Thorsten Fink's exit, with the club second-to-last after seven matchdays on four points, according to Austrian outlet LAOLA1.
Turkish media report that Bjelica has not solved Samsunspor's problems, having lost his first match in charge 4-1.
Turkish outlet Gazetevatan reports a bleak picture at Samsunspor after consecutive poor results, with the club's board and fans alarmed by the threat of relegation.
Samsunspor's Jaures Assoumou is back in contention after a spell out with a hamstring injury, according to Turkish media.
Samsunspor are preparing for the Amed match under Bjelica with sessions at the Nuri Asan facilities, including a small-sided game.
Amed coach Besnik Hasi said the Samsunspor and Eyüpspor matches are more important to him right now than the Galatasaray match.
